goal: Adds a doc/notifications.md page documenting the -blocknotify, -walletnotify, -alertnotify, -startupnotify and -shutdownnotify options and their threading/ordering behavior.
Fills a gap where these behaviors were only discoverable by reading source code.

result.summary: This PR adds a new doc/notifications.md file documenting Bitcoin Core's shell-command notification options (-blocknotify, -walletnotify, -alertnotify, -startupnotify, -shutdownnotify), focusing on cross-cutting threading and ordering behavior not covered in --help text. It also links the new doc from doc/README.md. The doc was distilled from an initial exhaustive version down to a single paragraph on threading/ordering plus a list of options, per reviewer feedback.
result.problem: The five -*notify options have undiscoverable behaviors (IBD suppression, lack of ordering guarantees across notifications, threading model) that are only visible by reading source code, making it hard for operators and integrators to build reliable tooling around them. This partially addresses long-standing issue #14278 requesting such documentation.

open_concerns: sedited raised on 2026-09-16 whether the PR should guarantee ordering at all, calling it 'a brittle thing to be promising,' and asked whether anyone has actually complained about ordering since the original issue.

willcl-ark is comparing against his own competing draft (callback-docs-cleanup) that takes a different framing (never guaranteeing notification legitimacy) and mentions adding tests for guarantees, raising the possibility of a larger rework or a redirect to his branch.
resolved_concerns: Initial exhaustive per-option documentation was replaced with a distilled paragraph on threading/ordering plus an option list, per sedited's first review comment; author implemented this in a force-push.
sedited's follow-up nits (ZMQ comparison sentence, em-dash, unsupported ordering claim about -shutdownnotify) were all addressed by the author in the 2026-06-30 push.
sedited gave an ACK on 2026-07-23 after the revisions.

This is a live, unresolved design question about what the doc should actually claim, raised after the ACK, and the author has not yet responded (last author activity 2026-06-30, well before this reopening).  Reviewing the current text is not wasted, but a substantive rewrite following this discussion looks plausible.

categories.name: docs
categories.evidence: The PR's sole change is adding doc/notifications.md and linking it from doc/README.md, matching the docs category's path and label priors exactly.
categories.rationale: P3 because it documents previously undiscoverable behavior (IBD suppression, ordering, threading model) for options that operators and integrators rely on to build external tooling, per the description 'several behaviors are only discoverable by reading the source.' It partially addresses a long-open issue (#14278) and is referenced by a related merged doc PR (#35586), showing real interest in this documentation gap, but the scope is narrow (one small doc file) and the current ordering-guarantee framing is now disputed, so its final content may change materially.

uncertainties: Whether willcl-ark's parallel branch will supersede this PR or whether this PR will simply be revised to incorporate his framing and tests is unclear from the discussion.
No explicit maintainer decision yet on whether ordering should be documented as a guarantee at all, which could change the doc's content substantially before merge.
result.card: This PR adds doc/notifications.md, documenting the -blocknotify, -walletnotify, -alertnotify, -startupnotify, and -shutdownnotify shell-command options, focusing on threading and ordering behavior not covered in --help text, partially addressing long-open issue #14278. The author revised the doc per reviewer sedited's request, distilling an initial exhaustive version to a short paragraph plus an option list, and received an ACK from sedited on 2026-07-23. However, on 2026-09-15/16 sedited and willcl-ark reopened a substantive question about whether the doc's ordering-guarantee framing is appropriate, with willcl-ark referencing his own competing draft that adds tests for such guarantees; the author has not responded to this newer discussion. This is a small, low-risk documentation PR whose value is filling a real, previously source-only documentation gap for operators and integrators, but its final framing may still change given the unresolved scope question.
